name: Perceptions of Washington State Streets: nature quality, beauty, relaxation and safety slider comparisons
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (96 new straight-ahead Google Street View views of Washington State, captured 2017–2026, © Google: half from Seattle, the rest from Tacoma, Spokane and Vancouver plus the small towns Ellensburg, Port Angeles and Walla Walla). Based on Larkin, Krishna, Chen, Amram, Avery, Duncan & Hystad, "Measuring and modelling perceptions of the built environment for epidemiological research using crowd-sourcing and image-based deep learning models" (Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology, 2022). Each original Mechanical Turk survey had five comparisons in random order: nature quality, beauty, relaxation, safety and a quality-check question on which image has more cars. Participants moved a slider towards the chosen street, farther for stronger feelings, with no tie allowed; slider strength fed a multinomial TrueSkill score. Over 36,000 comparisons were collected for images sampled to match where Washington State Twin Registry members live. This template runs three such rounds (15 comparisons) per participant and stores each slider position (−50 to +50).

Differences from the original study: (1) images are 96 random street views, not the paper's images selected from 117,374 GSV views to balance scene composition; (2) only straight-ahead views are used, while the original showed straight or side views (the same angle within a survey); (3) three rounds per participant instead of one five-comparison survey per paid task; (4) image pairs are drawn at random instead of the paper's adaptive pairing by TrueSkill uncertainty; (5) the car check cannot be scored automatically because the images were not chosen as with-car / without-car pairs; (6) only the nature-quality question wording is quoted in the paper, so the beauty, relaxation and safety wordings are ours.
author: Larkin, Krishna, Chen, Amram, Avery, Duncan & Hystad
